          Man Utd 4th, Spurs 12th, Newcastle 20th? Premier League Expected Points Table After Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re five games into the 2026-27 Premier League season. That gives us some data to work with, but it’s still a small enough sample for luck and variance to have played a significant role in the results. So, which teams have been fortunate, and which might feel hard done by?
Is the early-season Premier League table lying to us?

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit top as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind. Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, round out the top four.
Tottenham prop up the table, sitting bottom of the league with just two points. Fulham and Coventry City join them in the relegation zone.

In many ways, absolutely. The table is a perfect reflection of how matches have gone so far this season. The aim of the game is to win football matches, and there is no more hard-hitting proof of success than the league table.
In other ways, though, it might be slightly skewed. Some teams might feel they have performed better than their results suggest. For others, the opposite might be true.
This is where Opta’s expected points model can add a little more nuance.

The expected points model simulates the number of goals scored by each side in each match based on the expected goals (xG) value of every shot taken. It then uses those simulated goal totals to determine the outcome of the match, whether that is a win, draw or defeat. Each match is simulated 10,000 times.
The expected points for each team can then be calculated based on the proportion of simulations they win, draw or lose.

We’re aware this is not an exact science. Expected goals data doesn’t account for every factor at play during a football match, including game state and dangerous periods of possession that don’t result in shots. We’re also very much aware that real points matter infinitely more than expected ones.
Nevertheless, the expected points table can give us some interesting additional context on what we have seen across the opening five matchdays.
The first major talking point is that Arsenal sit top of the expected points table.

They remain favourites to win the title according to the Opta supercomputer, and their underlying numbers are still strong. They have the highest expected goals difference (+4.44) of any side in the Premier League.

Man City are second according to the expected points model. They have made a hugely impressive start under new manager Enzo Maresca, but the model suggests they have collected 5.8 more points than the underlying data from the chances they have created and conceded would normally warrant.

Sunderland generated 3.57 expected goals against them on MD5, the third-highest figure ever recorded (since 2013-14) by a losing team in a Premier League game, while the chances in City’s game against Manchester United (won 1-0) were essentially even.

There is important context to add here, though. City have spent a greater proportion of their game time leading (52.5%) than any other Premier League side this season. That means they have had less need to chase matches and push numbers forward, which could naturally reduce their overall xG output.

That’s something we need to bear in mind when analysing the expected points table, and one of the model’s limitations. A team protecting a lead doesn’t necessarily need to generate chances at the same rate as one searching for a goal.
So, which teams might feel they should be higher up the league?

Michael Carrick has come in for plenty of criticism following Manchester United’s poor start to the season. United have taken just five points from their opening five league games, their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign alongside 2014-15.

Their underlying numbers, however, are far more encouraging. United lead the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). Their total xG of 9.89 is the fourth-highest in the division.
